## 3. version-metadata status: inference, NOT proof
what public evidence shows:
- at 93d5a726 the committed tree says client/package.json 2.1.18-1 and client/Cargo.toml 2.1.18 (archive verified)
- npm 2.1.19-1 published 2025-12-22T20:17:01Z, 3h43m after 93d5a726 was committed (16:34:27Z)
- exhaustive history check (git log --all -S'2.1.19', 2 hits): committed 2.1.19-1 EXISTS, introduced by 84db4cf "completely redo github action flow" (2026-01-09, 18 days AFTER the npm publish) and removed by 9cde724 (2.1.19-1 -> 2.1.20-1). no commit carries 2.1.19-1 together with the info.commit 93d5a726; the committed 2.1.19-1 trees (84db4cf..0c11678d) also contain later source changes (e.g. 97cd1825 panic fix)
- the repo's CI release workflow only landed 2026-01-09/10, after this publish
supported inference (hypothesis, not proof): the published 2.1.19-1 was built at 93d5a726 with an uncommitted publish-time version-string bump, later committed retroactively at 84db4cf.
NOT established by public evidence:
- that the version string was the ONLY uncommitted change (hypothesis only). npm records gitHead from HEAD regardless of working-tree dirt, so other uncommitted changes cannot be excluded.
- therefore this packet does NOT claim the carried binary's behavior is entirely determined by the 93d5a726 source, and no NOTICE/README text may say so.
what would close the gap (finite routes investigated):
- publisher attestation of the publish-time tree state: not found (no npm provenance attestation - dist.attestations is null; the registry signature is npm's own package signature, not publish provenance; no git tag or GitHub release exists for 2.1.19-1 - the only tag/release is "latest", a 2026-10-23 continuous build at 9cde724)
rebuild attempt EXECUTED (bounded, one dated toolchain, no version matrix): real clone checkout at 93d5a726 (git rev-parse HEAD verified), RUSTUP_TOOLCHAIN=nightly-2025-12-22 (rustc 1.94.0-nightly a6525d526 2025-12-21, the publish-day nightly), wasm-bindgen CLI 0.2.100 (prebuilt), wasm-opt binaryen version_125 (newest release predating the publish). RESULT: cargo build fails in core - "panic_immediate_abort is now a real panic strategy" - meaning build.sh's -Zbuild-std-features=panic_immediate_abort is rejected by this nightly. the latest nightly (1.101.0-nightly 2026-10-29) fails identically. toolchain-window evidence (public, no build): rust-lang/rust PR 146317 "Add panic=immediate-abort" (https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/146317, merged 2025-09-23, merge 405608236020) converted build-std-features=panic_immediate_abort into a compile_error in core (verified in its patch: the old const-assert became compile_error!) - so the committed build.sh fails on the two tested post-merge nightlies (merge date approximates, not proves, the nightly cutoff), and works with flag adaptation. PR 147470 (https://github.com/rust-lang/rust/pull/147470, merged 2025-10-09) clarified the remediation text attempt B hit, and notes -Cpanic=immediate-abort alone is insufficient (build-std still required, which build.sh already does). CONSTRAINT: the shipped binary was not reproduced by the committed build.sh on the publish-day or current nightly. IF the publisher used the committed build.sh, their setup differed (older nightly or adjusted flags); other unknown build setups are not ruled out. OPTION-2 RESULT (executed, see rebuild/RESULT.md): one documented flag-adapted build on nightly-2025-12-22 SUCCEEDED but produced sha256 337afcb0..., a MISMATCH vs the carried binary (4e26f08f...) - per the pre-set rule this is inconclusive: correspondence remains an evidence-supported lead, not proven, not disproven. no further builds without a new authorized route.
